title: Elastomeric PGS Scaffolds in Arterial Tissue Engineering
protocol: Prepare glass tubing as a mold for scaffold.
Dissolve 100 mg of hyaluronic acid (HA) in 10 ml of deionized water to prepare a 1.0 wt/vol % HA solution.
Mix the HA solution using a rotator overnight until there are no air bubbles in the solution.
Pour the 1.0% HA solution into the top of glass tubing and let it flow slowly down along the inner wall of the mold.
Flip over the tubing when the solution reaches the bottom and repeat this step until the inner wall is evenly coated by the solution.
Dry all glass tubings in a vacuum oven at 37°C for 24 hours.
Grind salt particles to a size of 25-32 μm.
Assemble a glass tubing (coated with 1.0% HA inside), mandrel, heat-shrinkable sleeve, and PTFE ring as described previously.
Add salt particles to the glass mold using a spatula through a silicon rubber funnel.
Tap the mold gently to ensure even distribution of salt particles.
Scrape off excess salt particles across the top of the mold using the side of spatula.
Turn on the hybridization incubator for 30 minutes before transferring the salt-packed mold.
Transfer the salt-packed mold into the hybridization incubator.
Remove the molds from the hybridization incubator.
Dry the molds in a vacuum oven at 37°C for 24 hours.
Take the salt-packed molds out of the vacuum oven and allow them to cool to room temperature.
Push down on the stainless steel mandrel with one hand while holding the PTFE ring to remove it.
If the mandrel is tight, use needle pliers to pull it out.
Remove the PTFE ring from the bottom of the mold.
Place the molds into an oven at 120°C for 5 minutes to shrink the HS sleeve.
Check if the HS sleeve has shrunk properly.
Take off the HS sleeve from the salt-packed molds and let them cool to room temperature.
Store the molds in a desiccator until use.
Dissolve 3 g of PGS into 15 ml of THF to create a 20 wt/vol % solution.
Add the PGS solution to the lumen of salt-packed molds using a pipette in a fume hood.
Lean the glass mold at approximately 45 degrees and drop the PGS solution slowly while rotating the mold.
Ensure that the PGS solution flows down along the wall of the mold; add more solution if dry spots are observed.
Place the molds in the fume hood for at least 30 minutes to evaporate THF.
Put the molds into a vacuum oven for curing at 100 mTorr and 150°C for a predetermined time (e.g., 24, 36, or 48 hours).
Take out the molds after curing.
Place the molds at room temperature to cool down.
Dip each mold into deionized water slowly in a vertical position.
Transfer the molds to the water bath carefully, placing them at an angle for 1 hour using a silicon tube.
Check if hyaluronic acid (HA) is dissolved from the mold.
If no HA is released, push one end of the scaffold slowly using a spatula to release it from the mold.
Repeat the step at the other end of the scaffold and shake the mold back and forth slowly in the water bath.
Transfer the scaffold to another water bath with stirrer carefully.
Place the scaffold in the water bath for at least 3 days, changing water daily to leach out salt particles.
After leaching out salt particles, transfer each scaffold to a 15 ml centrifuge tube filled with deionized water.
Place the tubes in the dry-ice box for 1 hour to freeze.
Put the centrifuge tubes into the lyophilizer and lyophilize them for 2 days with all tube cabs opened.
Transfer the scaffolds to a dessicator until they are used.
Take out scaffolds from the dessicator and cut them to 25-30 mm in length.
Prepare two silicone rubber stoppers with a diameter of 20 mm, wall thickness of 6.35 mm, and middle hole diameter of 3 mm.
Connect two PTFE tubings (outer diameter = 3.97 mm, inner diameter = 2.38 mm, wall thickness = 0.79 mm, lengths = 60 mm and 40 mm) through the middle holes of each stopper.
Cut a HS ring to a length of 1.5 mm and place it on one end of the scaffold.
Push one PTFE tubing (connected silicone rubber stopper) into one end of the scaffold with minimal overlap.
Place the scaffold and PTFE tubing assembly in an oven at 120 °C for 10 minutes to shrink the HS ring.
Check if the HS ring is shrunk and the scaffolds are firmly connected to the PTFE tubing.
Remove the scaffold and PTFE tubing from the oven and allow them to cool down to room temperature.
Insert the scaffold-PTFE tubing assembly into a polycarbonate tube (outer diameter = 15.5 mm, inner diameter = 9 mm, length = 50 mm) as a bioreactor chamber.
Connect the other end of PTFE tubing to the scaffold following previous steps.
Attach two silicone rubber stoppers to both ends of the polycarbonate tube by aligning their inner surfaces with the tube ends.
Secure both outer surfaces of the silicone rubber stoppers to aluminum alloy plates (width = 20 mm, length = 70 mm, thickness = 6.35 mm) using threaded rods and tighten thumb nut screws on the plate.
Measure the seedable length of each scaffold between two HS rings.
Calculate the inner surface area of each scaffold for cell seeding using π x inner diameter x seedable length.
Wrap one bioreactor chamber unit with aluminum foil.
Autoclave the wrapped bioreactor chamber unit at 120 °C for 30 min to sterilize it.
Sterilize the medium reservoir by autoclaving at 120 °C for 30 min.
Sterilize the pump tubing by autoclaving at 120 °C for 30 min.
Sterilize the gas exchanger by autoclaving at 120 °C for 30 min.
Sterilize the manifolds by autoclaving at 120 °C for 30 min.
Sterilize the needle valve by autoclaving at 120 °C for 30 min.
Assemble each sterilized part of the bioreactor inside the cell culture hood.
Pre-treat scaffolds with a series of perfusions starting with 70% ethanol for 1 h.
Continue pre-treatment with 50% ethanol for 1 h.
Proceed with 25% ethanol perfusion for 1 h.
Rinse scaffolds with phosphate-buffered saline (PBS) for 2 h.
Further rinse scaffolds with SMC culture medium for 24 h using a peristaltic pump at 1.0 ml/min in the flow circuit.
Isolate primary arterial smooth muscle cells (SMCs) from carotid arteries of juvenile male baboons.
Characterize isolated SMCs in two-dimensional (2D) culture before passaging and seeding as described previously.
Expand SMCs using MCDB 131 medium with 10% fetal bovine serum, 1% L-glutamine, 50 μg/ml ascorbic acid, and an antibiotic-antimycotic solution.
Detach each bioreactor chamber from the flow circuit in the bioreactor.
Seed SMCs (passage 4-6) to the scaffold with a density of 2x10^6 cells/cm² by injecting suspension with a 5 ml syringe into the lumen of scaffolds after cutting off both abluminal and luminal flows.
Put all bioreactor chambers into the hybridization incubator at 37 °C and rotate them at 2 rpm for 4 h to allow the cells to uniformly spread into the scaffold.
Take out bioreactor chambers from the hybridization incubator and reattach them to the flow circuit of the bioreactor in the hood.
Transfer all bioreactor system into the cell culture incubator.
Connect pump tubing (inner diameter = 1.6 mm) to the cartilage of peristaltic pump and load fresh culture medium in the reservoir.
Start through-wall perfusion (luminal to abluminal) at 1.0 ml/min for 15 min followed by luminal flow only.
Increase the flow rate and pressure gradually from 1.0 ml/min (luminal shear stress: 1.1 dynes/cm²) and 20 mmHg on day 1 to 14.2 ml/min (15.3 dynes/cm²) and 120 mmHg on day 21, respectively.
Change the pump tubing (inner diameter = 3.2 mm) at day 4.
Change the medium once every week.
After 21-day culture, stop the pump and clamp tubings (inlet and outlet) of the medium reservoir.
Detach pump tubing from the cartilage of peristaltic pump.
Transfer bioreactor system into the hood.
Clamp inlet and outlet tubings of each bioreactor chamber.
Detach the chamber from the flow loop.
Open the inlet tubing.
Prepare a petri-dish at the outlet tubing to collect culture medium inside the polycarbonate tube.
Open the outlet tubing slowly and remove the medium from the chamber.
Detach the abluminal gauge needle and luminal silicone tubing from the chamber.
Release thumb screws to detach aluminum plates.
Remove the polycarbonate tube.
Detach one end of the tissue construct from the PTFE tubing.
Prepare a petri-dish filled with 10 ml of PBS.
Detach the other end of the construct from the PTFE tubing.
Put the construct into the PBS and rinse three times.
Cut the construct with a razor blade as 5-mm lengths.
Freeze the construct at -80 °C freezer for biochemical assay.
Transfer the construct to a 15 ml centrifuge tube filled with 5 ml of fresh medium for mechanical testing.
Snap freeze the construct into Tissue-Tek optimal cutting temperature compound for histology/immunofluorescence staining.
Seed SMCs into each bioreactor chamber.
Rotate the bioreactor chamber at 37°C for 4 hours after seeding to distribute cells uniformly in the scaffold lumen.
Apply pulsatile flow to scaffolds starting from day 1 with gradually increasing flow rate and pressure over days.
Maintain constant flow and pressure until the end of culture on day 21.
Examine surface morphology of the PGS scaffold by scanning electron microscopy (SEM).
Measure morphometric parameters of the scaffold using microcomputed tomography (micro-CT) and imaging analysis.
Examine cellular morphology of the PGS construct by SEM.
Check for multilayered SMCs covering the luminal surface perpendicularly oriented to flow direction.
Evaluate presence of ECM and elastic fibers using H&E staining and elastin autofluorescence.
Measure production of ECM proteins from biochemical assays.
